result_text:
`Tool.from_function(fn)` and `FunctionTool.from_function(fn)` now use the metadata the `@tool` decorator attached to `fn`. Your example gives name `custom-greet`, description `Greets people`, and the decorator's version, title, tags and meta. The tests in `tests/tools` pass (306 passed, 1 skipped). I haven't run the full suite or `prek`, and I didn't add a test for the new behaviour. My only check of the decorator case was a throwaway script with an example like yours.

The change is in `FunctionTool.from_function` in `src/fastmcp/tools/function_tool.py`. `Tool.from_function` just forwards to it with no arguments, so it needed no edit.

The new lookup runs only when no `metadata` and no individual metadata arguments are passed, and only if `fn.__fastmcp__` is a `ToolMeta`. Everything else behaves as before. That includes explicit `metadata=` or keyword arguments (nothing is merged in), the error when both are given, and functions with no decorator metadata or a non-`ToolMeta` `__fastmcp__`.

All `ToolMeta` fields are honoured, not just the six you listed.
